zh:
1900 年，Bachelier 在博士论文里要解决一件具体的事：给巴黎交易所里买卖的期权定价。要定价，先得说清楚到期那天价格落在各个位置的概率。他的办法是把价格变动看成一连串互相独立的随机增量，比爱因斯坦关于布朗运动的论文还早五年。六十年后，Fama 和 Samuelson 给了它一个经济学上的理由：如果价格已经反映了所有已知的信息，它的下一步变动就只能来自还没人知道的新消息，也就无从预测。

这就是"独立同分布"的世界：每一步的收益都从同一个分布里重新抽，与过去无关。分布可以换。正态最温和；Student-t 和混合正态有厚尾，对应 Mandelbrot 1963 年在棉花价格里看到的现象：极端的变动比正态分布预言的多得多；两点分布是给期权定价时最简单的模型：每一步价格只有涨、跌两种可能。
en:
In 1900, Bachelier set out in his doctoral thesis to solve a concrete problem: pricing the options traded on the Paris Bourse. To price them, you first have to spell out the probability that the price ends up at each level on the expiration date. His approach was to treat price changes as a sequence of mutually independent random increments, five years before Einstein's paper on Brownian motion. Sixty years later, Fama and Samuelson gave it an economic justification: if the price already reflects all known information, its next move can only come from news that nobody knows yet, and so it cannot be predicted.

This is the "i.i.d." world: the return at each step is drawn anew from the same distribution, independently of the past. The distribution can be changed. The normal is the mildest. Student-t and the normal mixture have heavy tails, corresponding to what Mandelbrot saw in cotton prices in 1963: extreme moves are far more frequent than the normal distribution predicts. The two-point distribution is the simplest model used in pricing options: at each step the price has only two possibilities, up or down.

zh:
把它当作对照组。这里过去不含未来的任何信息，所以任何择时的规则（根据对涨跌的判断决定什么时候持有、什么时候空仓）按长期增长率都不该赢过平均仓位和它相同的固定比例。一条不加杠杆的规则如果在这里显著赢了基准，要么是从很多次尝试里挑出来的运气，要么是代码用到了未来的数据。固定在 1 到 3 倍之间的仓位会赢（固定 2 倍每年多赚 1.6 个百分点；越靠近 3 倍优势越小，算上换手成本，到 2.8 倍左右就没有了），但那只是加了杠杆。仓位忽大忽小的规则未必赢：默认参数的"线性均值回复"在 −1 和 3 两头来回跳，结果栏的"平均仓位"（按绝对值算）是 1.7，每年反而少 10 个百分点上下。和平均仓位（带正负号算）相同的固定比例比，它不会更好。

也用它看厚尾对杠杆的影响：把分布从正态换成 Student-t，同样的仓位，破产的路径多出来多少。
en:
Use it as the control group. Here the past contains no information about the future, so no timing rule (one that decides when to hold and when to be flat according to its view of whether the price will rise or fall) should beat, measured by long-run growth rate, the fixed fraction with the same average position. If a rule that uses no leverage significantly beats the benchmark here, either it is luck picked out of many attempts, or the code used data from the future. A position fixed between 1× and 3× does win (a fixed 2× earns 1.6 percentage points more per year; the closer to 3×, the smaller the advantage, and once turnover costs are counted it is gone at about 2.8×), but that is only leverage. A rule whose position swings between large and small does not necessarily win: with default parameters, "Linear mean reversion" jumps back and forth between the two ends, −1 and 3; its "Average position" in the results bar (computed from absolute values) is 1.7, yet it earns about 10 percentage points less per year. Compared with the fixed fraction that has the same average position (computed with signs), it does no better.

Also use it to see the effect of heavy tails on leverage: switch the distribution from normal to Student-t and see how many more paths are ruined at the same position.

zh: 只有仓位大小这一件事可做：固定比例，取 Kelly 比例附近或者更保守。厚尾和负偏都会让最优的比例变小。
en: There is only one thing to decide, the position size: a fixed fraction, near the Kelly fraction or more conservative. Heavy tails and negative skew both make the optimal fraction smaller.

zh: 规则选"均线交叉"或"时间序列动量"：它们显著输给买入持有。不是因为预测反了：均线交叉有一半的时间空仓，时间序列动量（默认允许做空）有一半的时间在做空，都白白放弃了正的漂移，还要付成本。
en: Choose the rule "Moving-average crossover" or "Time-series momentum": they significantly underperform buy and hold. This is not because their predictions are backward: moving-average crossover is flat half the time, and time-series momentum (which allows shorting by default) is short half the time; both give up the positive drift for nothing, and pay costs as well.

zh: 分布换成"Student-t"，自由度调到 3，规则选"固定比例"，仓位调到 2：两千条路径里有几条一步亏光，长期增长率变成 −∞。正态分布下，同样的仓位一条也不会。
en: Switch the distribution to "Student-t", set the degrees of freedom to 3, choose the rule "Fixed fraction" and set the position to 2: a few of the two thousand paths lose everything in a single step, and the long-run growth rate becomes −∞. Under the normal distribution, not a single path does so at the same position.

zh: 打开"单步收益分布"，在正态和 Student-t 之间切换，看尾巴。
en: Open "One-step return distribution" and switch between normal and Student-t; look at the tails.

zh:
最干净的下注问题：一枚硬币，胜率 p，赢了净得赌注的 b 倍，输了失去赌注。Kelly 1956 年正是用这个模型推出了他的公式。数学家 Thorp 在 60 年代带着这个公式走进赌场算 21 点：牌堆里剩下的大牌多时，这一把对他有百分之一上下的优势。知道自己占优之后，剩下的问题是：手里的筹码该押上多大一部分？后来他又带着同一个公式去了华尔街。

在这个世界里，"仓位"就是每次押上的资金比例。十套玩法里的"③ 偏硬币下注"是同一枚硬币的另一种问法：那里照搬一个真实的实验，有封顶、有次数，得分是平均带走多少美元；这里不封顶，按三种口径看增长率。
en:
The cleanest betting problem: a coin with win probability p; if you win, you net b times the stake, and if you lose, you lose the stake. It was with exactly this model that Kelly derived his formula in 1956. In the 1960s the mathematician Thorp took the formula into the casinos to count cards at blackjack: when many high cards remained in the deck, the hand gave him an edge of about one percent. Once he knew he had the edge, the remaining question was: what fraction of the chips in his hand should he stake? Later he took the same formula to Wall Street.

In this world, the "position" is the fraction of capital staked on each flip. "③ Betting on a biased coin" among the ten games is another question about the same coin: there a real experiment is copied as it was, with a cap and a limited number of flips, and the score is the average number of dollars taken home; here there is no cap, and the growth rate is judged by the three criteria.

zh: 只想研究"押多大"这一个问题、不想被别的东西干扰的时候。它也是理解杠杆曲线最快的地方：增长率 $g(f)=p\log(1+bf)+(1-p)\log(1-f)$ 有精确的公式，可以和模拟逐点对照。
en: When you want to study the single question of "how much to stake" without being distracted by anything else. It is also the quickest place to understand the leverage curve: the growth rate $g(f)=p\log(1+bf)+(1-p)\log(1-f)$ has an exact formula, which can be compared with the simulation point by point.

zh: 固定比例 $f^*=p-(1-p)/b$。别的押法（输了加倍、赢了加注）都不会更好：硬币没有记忆。
en: The fixed fraction $f^*=p-(1-p)/b$. No other way of betting (doubling after a loss, raising the stake after a win) does better: the coin has no memory.

zh: 把左栏"规则"下面的"仓位比例 f"从 0.05 慢慢拖到 0.5（这个世界里，仓位就是每次押上资金的比例），看增长率先升后降；打开"杠杆曲线"看整条曲线。
en: Drag "Position fraction f" under "Rule" in the left column slowly from 0.05 to 0.5 (in this world, the position is the fraction of capital staked on each flip) and watch the growth rate rise and then fall; open "Leverage curve" to see the whole curve.

zh: 规则换成"输了加倍"，打开"终值分布"：多数路径赚得不少（中位数约 4 倍），约五分之一的路径归零。
en: Switch the rule to "Double after a loss" and open "Terminal wealth distribution": most paths make a good profit (the median is about 4×), and about one fifth of the paths go to zero.

zh: 把赔率 b 改成 2、胜率改成 0.4：每一次的期望仍然是正的，Kelly 比例是 0.1。
en: Change the odds b to 2 and the win probability to 0.4: the expectation of each flip is still positive, and the Kelly fraction is 0.1.

zh:
Bachelier 的模型有个毛病：价格可以变成负数。1965 年 Samuelson 把它改成了"几何"的：不是价格本身、而是价格的对数在做布朗运动，于是价格永远为正，涨跌按比例算。Black、Scholes 和 Merton 的期权定价理论就建在它上面。

Merton 1969 年在这个世界里问的，是每个有积蓄的人都会遇到的问题：钱分成两份，一份存银行拿固定的利息，一份买股票，比例该是多少，要不要随着涨跌调整？在这个世界里，答案是一个不随时间变的比例。

它只有两个参数：漂移 μ 是平均每年涨多少，波动 σ 是不确定性有多大。
en:
Bachelier's model has a flaw: the price can become negative. In 1965 Samuelson made it "geometric": it is not the price itself but the logarithm of the price that follows a Brownian motion, so the price is always positive, and rises and falls are measured proportionally. The option pricing theory of Black, Scholes and Merton is built on it.

What Merton asked in this world in 1969 is a question that everyone with savings faces: the money is split into two parts, one deposited in a bank to earn fixed interest and one used to buy stocks; what should the proportion be, and should it be adjusted as prices rise and fall? In this world, the answer is a proportion that does not change over time.

It has only two parameters: the drift μ is how much the price rises per year on average, and the volatility σ is how large the uncertainty is.

zh: 默认的起点，也是一切"有没有规律"的对照组。这里价格没有记忆，择时无效，所有的问题都归结为仓位。练习读扇形图和杠杆曲线、体会标准误，用它最合适；检验一个模型会不会无中生有，也用它。
en: The default starting point, and the control group for every "is there a pattern?" question. Here the price has no memory, market timing does not work, and every question comes down to the position. It is the best place to practice reading the fan chart and the leverage curve and to get a feel for the standard error; also use it to test whether a model conjures something out of nothing.

zh: 固定比例 $f^*=(\mu-r_f)/\sigma^2$，这是 Merton 的结果。默认参数下 $f^*=2$，最优增长率是每年 8%。均线、动量、止损在这里都赢不了买入持有：它们付了成本，还错过了一部分漂移。
en: The fixed fraction $f^*=(\mu-r_f)/\sigma^2$; this is Merton's result. With default parameters $f^*=2$, and the optimal growth rate is 8% per year. Moving averages, momentum and stop-losses cannot beat buy and hold here: they pay costs, and they also miss part of the drift.

zh: 规则选"固定比例"，打开"杠杆曲线"：增长率的峰在 2 倍附近。把"交易设定"里的仓位上限调到 5：理论曲线在 4 倍处回到 0，模拟的曲线因为换手成本，在 3.8 倍上下就过零了。
en: Choose the rule "Fixed fraction" and open "Leverage curve": the growth rate peaks near 2×. Set the position cap in "Trading settings" to 5: the theoretical curve returns to 0 at 4×, while the simulated curve, because of turnover costs, already crosses zero at about 3.8×.

zh: 规则选"均线交叉"，对两根均线做二维的"参数扫描"，挑出最好的一格，再点"用新路径检验"。
en: Choose the rule "Moving-average crossover", run a two-dimensional "Parameter sweep" over the two moving averages, pick the best cell, then click "Test on fresh paths".

zh: 规则选"预测模型流水线"，模型换成"k 近邻"：训练集 R² 是正的，验证集 R² 是负的。它在拟合噪声。
en: Choose the rule "Prediction pipeline" and switch the model to "k-nearest neighbors": the training-set R² is positive, and the validation-set R² is negative. It is fitting noise.

zh:
1930 年，Uhlenbeck 和 Ornstein 用它描述布朗粒子的速度：粒子被周围的分子随机撞击，同时受到一个与速度成正比的摩擦力，把它拉回静止。写成方程就是朗之万方程。

金融里，凡是有一股力量把价格拉回某个水平的地方都用得上它。一个典型的场景：两家业务几乎相同的公司，股价长期同涨同跌。某个月其中一家多涨了 8%，找不出任何理由。有人卖出涨多的、买入涨少的，等两者的价差回去（这叫配对交易）。他要知道的是：价差一般多久回去一半，偏离多少才值得动手。利率（Vasicek 1977）和商品价格也常用它来描述。参数 κ 是拉回去的速度，$\ln 2/\kappa$ 是偏离缩小一半所需的时间。
en:
In 1930, Uhlenbeck and Ornstein used it to describe the velocity of a Brownian particle: the particle is struck at random by the surrounding molecules and at the same time is subject to a friction force proportional to its velocity, which pulls it back to rest. Written as an equation, it is the Langevin equation.

In finance, it is useful wherever some force pulls the price back to a certain level. A typical scenario: two companies with almost identical businesses, whose stock prices rise and fall together over the long run. In some month one of them rises 8% more than the other, for no reason that anyone can find. Someone sells the one that rose more, buys the one that rose less, and waits for the spread between the two to revert (this is called pairs trading). What they need to know is how long the spread usually takes to revert halfway, and how large a deviation is worth acting on. Interest rates (Vasicek 1977) and commodity prices are also often described with it. The parameter κ is the speed at which it is pulled back, and $\ln 2/\kappa$ is the time it takes for a deviation to shrink by half.

zh: 研究"低买高卖"这一类规则的时候。它是均值回复规则的主场，也是趋势规则的客场：在这里追涨杀跌，方向正好反了。
en: When you study rules of the "buy low, sell high" kind. It is home turf for mean-reversion rules and an away game for trend rules: buying into rises and selling into falls here gets the direction exactly backward.

zh: 对数最优的仓位随偏离线性变化（"线性均值回复"这条规则）。有交易成本时，在一条带子之外才动手更好（"固定阈值带""z 分数带""网格"）。
en: The log-optimal position varies linearly with the deviation (the rule "Linear mean reversion"). With trading costs, it is better to act only outside a band ("Fixed threshold bands", "z-score bands", "Grid").

zh: 依次选"线性均值回复""均值回复（z 分数带）""时间序列动量"：增长率依次下降，动量是负的。
en: Choose "Linear mean reversion", "Mean reversion (z-score bands)" and "Time-series momentum" in turn: the growth rate falls from one to the next, and that of momentum is negative.

zh: 把回复速度 κ 从 5 调到 0.5（"线性均值回复"规则里的 κ 是"你的估计"，要手动改成同样的值）：半衰期从七周变成约 1.4 年，同样的规则赚得少得多。
en: Change the reversion speed κ from 5 to 0.5 (the κ in the rule "Linear mean reversion" is "your estimate", and has to be changed by hand to the same value): the half-life goes from seven weeks to about 1.4 years, and the same rule earns much less.

zh: 打开"自相关"：每个滞后上都只有 −0.01 上下（样本有四十万个点，所以仍然越过了虚线）；按它去预测，R² 只有万分之一。均值回复藏在价格的水平（价格本身的高低）里，不在相邻的收益里。
en: Open "Autocorrelation": it is only about −0.01 at every lag (the sample has four hundred thousand points, so it still crosses the dashed line); predicting from it gives an R² of only one ten-thousandth. The mean reversion is hidden in the level of the price (how high or low the price itself is), not in adjacent returns.

zh:
几何布朗运动里，价格是连续变动的：按每年 20% 的波动，一天跌掉 20% 这种事要等上比宇宙年龄还长的时间。可是 1987 年 10 月 19 日，标普 500 指数一天就跌了 20%。

Merton 1976 年的办法是在布朗运动上叠加"跳跃"：消息以随机的间隔到达（泊松过程），每来一条，价格瞬间跳一下，跳的幅度也是随机的。默认的参数是平均每年跳 3 次，每次平均向下 5%。
en:
In geometric Brownian motion the price moves continuously: at a volatility of 20% per year, you would have to wait longer than the age of the universe to see a fall of 20% in one day. Yet on October 19, 1987, the S&P 500 index fell 20% in a single day.

Merton's approach in 1976 was to superimpose "jumps" on the Brownian motion: news arrives at random intervals (a Poisson process), and each time a piece of news arrives the price jumps instantaneously, by an amount that is also random. The default parameters are 3 jumps per year on average, each 5% downward on average.

zh: 检验一条规则在突发事件面前是否脆弱。靠"盯着价格、跌到线就卖"来控制风险的规则，在跳空（价格不经过中间的价位，直接跳到另一个价）面前都会失灵：价格直接越过了止损线。加了杠杆的仓位在这里有真实的归零风险。
en: To test whether a rule is fragile in the face of sudden events. Rules that control risk by "watching the price and selling when it falls to the line" all fail in the face of a gap (the price jumps straight to another price without passing through the prices in between): the price goes straight past the stop-loss line. A leveraged position has a real risk of going to zero here.

zh: 仓位要比几何布朗运动里保守。跳的幅度没有下界时，严格地说只有不加杠杆（$0\le f\le1$）才永不破产。
en: The position should be more conservative than in geometric Brownian motion. When the jump size has no lower bound, strictly speaking only a position without leverage ($0\le f\le1$) is never ruined.

zh: 规则选"固定比例"，打开"杠杆曲线"，和漂移、波动相同的几何布朗运动比一比峰的位置。
en: Choose the rule "Fixed fraction", open "Leverage curve", and compare the position of the peak with that of a geometric Brownian motion with the same drift and volatility.

zh: 规则选"止损与再入场"，打开"单条路径明细"，换几条路径找一次大的下跳：止损是在跳完之后才执行的。
en: Choose the rule "Stop-loss and re-entry", open "Single-path detail", and go through a few paths to find a large downward jump: the stop-loss is executed only after the jump is over.

zh: 打开"单步收益分布"：左边的尾巴上多出一截。
en: Open "One-step return distribution": there is an extra piece on the left tail.

zh:
几何布朗运动假定波动是一个常数。实际的市场里，波动自己也在动：平静的时期和动荡的时期交替出现，而且下跌的时候波动往往上升。

谁需要关心这个？每天要回答"明天最多可能亏多少"的人。答案取决于明天的波动，而它和上个月不一样。

Heston 1993 年让方差自己成为一个均值回复的随机过程，并且允许它和价格相关。这个模型解释了期权市场上的"波动率微笑"：拿同一到期日、不同行权价的期权的市价，各自倒推出"市场认为的波动率"，画出来两头高、中间低；如果波动真是一个常数，这条线应该是平的。它因此成了期权定价的标准工具之一。
en:
Geometric Brownian motion assumes that volatility is a constant. In real markets, volatility itself moves: calm periods alternate with turbulent ones, and volatility tends to rise when prices fall.

Who needs to care about this? Anyone who has to answer, every day, "what is the most we could lose tomorrow?" The answer depends on tomorrow's volatility, which is not the same as last month's.

In 1993 Heston made the variance itself a mean-reverting stochastic process, and allowed it to be correlated with the price. This model explains the "volatility smile" in the options market: take the market prices of options with the same expiration date and different strike prices, back out from each one "the volatility the market believes in", and plot the results; they are high at both ends and low in the middle. If volatility really were a constant, this line would be flat. The model thus became one of the standard tools of option pricing.

zh: 研究风险管理类规则的时候：波动率目标、按波动调仓位。这里方向仍然不可预测，可预测的是波动的大小。
en: When you study risk-management rules: volatility targeting, adjusting the position according to volatility. Here the direction is still unpredictable; what is predictable is the size of the volatility.

zh: 对数最优的仓位与当前的方差成反比。"波动率目标"（与标准差成反比）方向是对的，只是反应不足。择时的规则在这里没有用。
en: The log-optimal position is inversely proportional to the current variance. "Volatility targeting" (inversely proportional to the standard deviation) goes in the right direction, but under-reacts. Timing rules are of no use here.

zh: 规则选"波动率目标"，和买入持有比：夏普略高（0.44 对 0.40），回撤的中位数从 16% 降到 14%；增长率略低，因为它的平均仓位不到 1。
en: Choose the rule "Volatility targeting" and compare it with buy and hold: the Sharpe ratio is slightly higher (0.44 versus 0.40), and the median drawdown falls from 16% to 14%; the growth rate is slightly lower, because its average position is below 1.

zh: 把相关系数 ρ 从 −0.7 改成 0：单步收益的分布几乎不变，买入持有最差的那 5% 的结局却明显好转。下跌和波动上升同时发生，伤害的是多步累积起来的结果。
en: Change the correlation ρ from −0.7 to 0: the distribution of one-step returns hardly changes, yet the worst 5% of outcomes for buy and hold improve markedly. When falls and rising volatility come together, what is hurt is the result accumulated over many steps.

zh: 打开"自相关"：收益本身不相关；收益的绝对值相关，而且衰减得慢。
en: Open "Autocorrelation": the returns themselves are uncorrelated; the absolute values of the returns are correlated, and the correlation decays slowly.

zh:
1982 年，Engle 研究英国的通货膨胀时注意到：预测误差的大小是成团出现的，一段时间都大，一段时间都小。他提出的 ARCH 模型，以及 Bollerslev 1986 年推广出的 GARCH，让今天的方差取决于昨天的冲击和昨天的方差。

Mandelbrot 更早就描述过这个现象：大的变动后面跟着大的变动，符号不定。它是金融时间序列里最稳固的经验事实之一，也是风险管理里估计"明天的波动"的标准办法。
en:
In 1982, while studying inflation in the United Kingdom, Engle noticed that the sizes of forecast errors come in clusters: large for a stretch of time, then small for a stretch of time. The ARCH model he proposed, and GARCH, Bollerslev's 1986 generalization of it, make today's variance depend on yesterday's shock and yesterday's variance.

Mandelbrot had described this phenomenon even earlier: large changes are followed by large changes, of either sign. It is one of the most robust empirical facts in financial time series, and also the standard way to estimate "tomorrow's volatility" in risk management.

zh: 和 Heston 一样，是"方向不可预测、波动可预测"的世界；区别是这里的波动由过去的收益直接决定，更容易从数据里估出来。用它检验波动率目标类的规则，以及带波动特征的预测模型。
en: Like Heston, it is a world where "the direction is unpredictable and the volatility is predictable"; the difference is that here the volatility is determined directly by past returns, and is easier to estimate from data. Use it to test rules of the volatility-targeting kind, and prediction models with volatility features.

zh: 理论上，按条件方差的倒数调仓位能提高增长率。实际能拿到多少，取决于波动起伏得有多厉害：默认的参数下起伏不大，好处和估计的噪声、交易成本差不多大。收益的无条件分布比正态厚尾，杠杆要保守。
en: In theory, scaling the position by the inverse of the conditional variance raises the growth rate. How much of this you actually get depends on how strongly the volatility fluctuates: with the default parameters the fluctuations are not large, and the benefit is about the same size as the estimation noise and the trading costs. The unconditional distribution of returns has heavier tails than the normal, so leverage should be conservative.

zh: 规则选"波动率目标"：默认参数下，夏普和买入持有分不出高低，回撤的中位数从 17% 降到 14%。
en: Choose the rule "Volatility targeting": with default parameters, its Sharpe ratio cannot be told apart from that of buy and hold, and the median drawdown falls from 17% to 14%.

zh: 把 α 调到 0.15、β 调到 0.84，让波动的起伏更大、更持久：波动率目标的夏普升到 0.5 以上，买入持有仍在 0.4 上下。
en: Set α to 0.15 and β to 0.84, so that the fluctuations in volatility are larger and more persistent: the Sharpe ratio of volatility targeting rises above 0.5, while buy and hold stays at about 0.4.

zh: 打开"单步收益分布"：峰度大于 3，虽然每一步的条件分布都是正态的。
en: Open "One-step return distribution": the kurtosis is greater than 3, even though the conditional distribution at every step is normal.

zh:
Hamilton 1989 年研究美国的经济周期时提出：经济在"扩张"和"衰退"两个状态之间切换，每个状态有自己的增长率；状态本身看不见，只能从数据里推断。

放到股市上，就是牛市和熊市：牛市慢慢涨、波动小，熊市跌得急、波动大，各自持续一段随机的时间。这是"趋势"在数学上最简单的来源：状态有惯性，所以过去的涨跌透露了现在处于哪个状态。
en:
In 1989, studying the US business cycle, Hamilton proposed that the economy switches between two states, "expansion" and "recession", each with its own growth rate; the state itself cannot be seen, and can only be inferred from the data.

Applied to the stock market, these are bull and bear markets: a bull market rises slowly with low volatility, a bear market falls fast with high volatility, and each lasts for a random length of time. This is mathematically the simplest source of "trend": the state has inertia, so past rises and falls reveal which state you are in now.

zh: 研究趋势跟踪为什么有时候管用。止损和波动率目标在这里是有价值的；均线交叉的收益和买入持有差不多，回撤却小得多；识别状态的模型（隐马尔可夫）假设的结构恰好就是这个世界真实的结构，赚得最多。也适合看风险管理值多少：躲开熊市比抓住牛市更要紧。
en: To study why trend following sometimes works. Stop-losses and volatility targeting have value here; moving-average crossover earns about the same return as buy and hold, but with a much smaller drawdown; the model that identifies the state (hidden Markov) assumes exactly the structure that this world really has, and it earns the most. It is also a good place to see how much risk management is worth: avoiding the bear market matters more than catching the bull market.

zh: 按"现在是牛市"的后验概率调仓位。均线交叉和止损是它粗糙的近似，隐马尔可夫模型是它精确的版本。
en: Setting the position according to the posterior probability that "this is a bull market now". Moving-average crossover and stop-losses are crude approximations of this; the hidden Markov model is the exact version.

zh: 依次选"买入持有""均线交叉""隐马尔可夫模型"：夏普比率从 0.61 升到 0.80，再到 1.6 上下。均线交叉的增长率和买入持有差不多，回撤的中位数却从 22% 降到 13%。
en: Choose "Buy and hold", "Moving-average crossover" and "Hidden Markov model" in turn: the Sharpe ratio rises from 0.61 to 0.80, and then to about 1.6. The growth rate of moving-average crossover is about the same as that of buy and hold, yet the median drawdown falls from 22% to 13%.

zh: 把牛市和熊市的平均时长分别调到 0.15 年和 0.05 年（比例不变，切换快了十倍）：趋势规则还没确认，状态就已经换了。均线交叉从和买入持有持平变成明显落后（每年 6.0% 对 9.3%）。不要把两个时长调成一样：那样平均漂移变成负的，任何少持仓的规则都会"显著好于基准"，那不是择时的功劳。
en: Set the average durations of the bull market and the bear market to 0.15 years and 0.05 years respectively (the ratio is unchanged, and switching is ten times faster): before a trend rule has confirmed the trend, the state has already changed. Moving-average crossover goes from level with buy and hold to clearly behind (6.0% per year versus 9.3%). Do not set the two durations equal: the average drift then becomes negative, and any rule that holds less will come out "Significantly better than the benchmark", but that is not thanks to market timing.

zh: 规则选"止损与再入场"：在这里止损是有价值的；换回几何布朗运动，同样的止损是负价值。
en: Choose the rule "Stop-loss and re-entry": here the stop-loss has value; switch back to geometric Brownian motion, and the same stop-loss has negative value.

zh:
最简单的"可以预测"的世界：这一步的收益里，有一小部分 φ 是上一步收益的延续（φ > 0，动量）或者反转（φ < 0）。它回答的是一个天天有人问的问题：昨天涨了 2%，今天该追，还是反着做？如果今天的收益里平均有十分之一是昨天的延续（φ = 0.1），答案是追，而且每天都值得按昨天的涨跌调一次仓。

现实里两种都有。Lo 和 MacKinlay 1988 年发现股指的周收益有正的自相关，推翻了"股价是随机游走"的简单版本。个股在几天到一个月的尺度上有反转，在几个月到一年的尺度上有动量（Jegadeesh & Titman 1993）。
en:
The simplest "predictable" world: of this step's return, a small fraction φ is a continuation of the previous step's return (φ > 0, momentum) or a reversal of it (φ < 0). It answers a question that someone asks every day: the price rose 2% yesterday, so should you chase it today, or do the opposite? If on average one tenth of today's return is a continuation of yesterday's (φ = 0.1), the answer is to chase, and it is worth rebalancing the position once a day according to yesterday's rise or fall.

In reality both occur. In 1988 Lo and MacKinlay found that the weekly returns of stock indexes have positive autocorrelation, overturning the simple version of "stock prices are a random walk". Individual stocks show reversal on scales of a few days to a month, and momentum on scales of a few months to a year (Jegadeesh & Titman 1993).

zh: 体会"预测力很弱也值钱"的地方。默认的 φ = 0.1 意味着 R² 只有 1%：每一步的走势里 99% 仍然是噪声，但不计成本时，按预测下注的年化夏普在 1.3 以上（理论值约 1.6）。中间的一步是：按预测的大小下注时，每一步的夏普约等于预测与实际的相关系数（IC，等于 $\sqrt{R^2}$），年化再乘 $\sqrt{252}$。这里 IC = φ = 0.1，$0.1\times\sqrt{252}\approx1.6$。它也是检验线性预测模型的标准场地：正确的答案就是线性回归。
en: The place to see that "even very weak predictive power is worth money". The default φ = 0.1 means that R² is only 1%: 99% of each step's move is still noise, yet when costs are ignored, the annualized Sharpe ratio of betting on the prediction is above 1.3 (the theoretical value is about 1.6). The step in between is this: when you bet in proportion to the size of the prediction, the Sharpe ratio of each step is approximately the correlation coefficient between the predicted and the actual values (the IC, equal to $\sqrt{R^2}$), and annualizing multiplies it by $\sqrt{252}$. Here IC = φ = 0.1, and $0.1\times\sqrt{252}\approx1.6$. It is also the standard testing ground for linear prediction models: the correct answer is linear regression.

zh: 仓位对最近一步的收益线性反应。"预测模型流水线"里的线性回归能把 φ 估出来，更复杂的模型不会更好。因为每一步都要调仓，交易成本在这里是决定性的。
en: A position that responds linearly to the return of the most recent step. The linear regression in "Prediction pipeline" can estimate φ, and more complex models do no better. Because the position has to be rebalanced at every step, trading costs are decisive here.

zh: 规则选"预测模型流水线"（线性回归），打开"模型诊断"：验证集 R² 应该在 1% 附近。
en: Choose the rule "Prediction pipeline" (linear regression) and open "Model diagnostics": the validation-set R² should be near 1%.

zh: 把交易成本从 5 个基点调到 0，再调到 20：这类每步都换仓的规则对成本极其敏感。
en: Change the trading cost from 5 basis points to 0, then to 20: rules of this kind, which change the position at every step, are extremely sensitive to costs.

zh: 把 φ 改成 −0.1："预测模型流水线"照样赚钱，它学到的系数跟着变了号；默认参数的"时间序列动量"则从略逊于基准（每年少一两个百分点，两千条路径上只有两三个标准误，刚看得出来）变成明显落后（每年少 12 个百分点）。
en: Change φ to −0.1: "Prediction pipeline" makes money all the same, and the coefficient it learns changes sign accordingly; "Time-series momentum" with default parameters, on the other hand, goes from slightly behind the benchmark (one or two percentage points less per year, only two or three standard errors on two thousand paths, barely visible) to clearly behind (12 percentage points less per year).

zh:
水文学家 Hurst 花了几十年研究尼罗河的水位记录，为的是算出水库该修多大。1951 年他发表了一个奇怪的发现：丰水年和枯水年成串出现的程度，远远超过独立的随机变量应有的样子，而且这种记忆在几十年、上百年的尺度上都不消失。

Mandelbrot 和 Van Ness 1968 年用"分数布朗运动"给它建了模。只有一个新参数 H：H = ½ 是普通的布朗运动；H > ½ 时增量长程正相关，趋势会持续；H < ½ 时长程负相关，来回震荡。
en:
The hydrologist Hurst spent decades studying the water-level records of the Nile, in order to work out how large a reservoir should be built. In 1951 he published a strange finding: wet years and dry years come in runs to a degree far beyond what independent random variables would show, and this memory does not disappear even on scales of decades or of a century and more.

In 1968 Mandelbrot and Van Ness modeled it with "fractional Brownian motion". There is only one new parameter, H: H = ½ is ordinary Brownian motion; when H > ½ the increments have long-range positive correlation, and trends persist; when H < ½ they have long-range negative correlation, and the path oscillates back and forth.

zh: 研究"长记忆"的时候：相关性不是集中在最近的一两步，而是薄薄地摊在很长的历史上。它检验的是规则和模型能不能利用很长的历史。
en: When you study "long memory": the correlation is not concentrated in the last one or two steps, but spread thinly over a very long history. What it tests is whether rules and models can make use of a very long history.

zh: H > ½ 时趋势类的规则管用，窗口可以取得比较长；H < ½ 时均值回复类的规则管用。最优的线性预测要用到全部历史。
en: When H > ½, trend rules work, and the window can be fairly long; when H < ½, mean-reversion rules work. The optimal linear prediction needs the entire history.

zh: 规则选"时间序列动量"，对窗口 n 做"参数扫描"：比起 AR(1) 世界，这里长窗口也有效。
en: Choose the rule "Time-series momentum" and run a "Parameter sweep" over the window n: compared with the AR(1) world, long windows also work here.

zh: 把 H 调到 0.35：动量由盈转亏，"均值回复（z 分数带）"由亏转盈。
en: Set H to 0.35: momentum turns from profit to loss, and "Mean reversion (z-score bands)" turns from loss to profit.

zh: 打开"自相关"：收益的自相关按幂律缓慢衰减，很多个滞后上都还看得见。
en: Open "Autocorrelation": the autocorrelation of returns decays slowly, as a power law, and is still visible at many lags.

zh:
1976 年，生物学家 May 在《自然》上发表了一篇文章，讲一个描述昆虫种群数量的方程：下一代的数量 = a × 这一代 ×（1 − 这一代）。方程简单到中学生都会算；可当 a 超过大约 3.57 之后，轨道不再重复，进入混沌（中间还夹着一些周期性的窗口）；到 a = 4，它产生的序列看上去完全是随机的。

这是"确定性混沌"最有名的例子：没有任何随机性，下一步完全由这一步决定，a = 4 时却通得过"是不是白噪声"的线性检验（a 小于 4 时相邻两项明显负相关，比如 a = 3.8 时相关系数约 −0.6）。这里把它的取值映射成了一个价格，默认 a = 4。
en:
In 1976 the biologist May published an article in Nature about an equation describing the size of an insect population: size of the next generation = a × this generation × (1 − this generation). The equation is so simple that a high-school student can compute it; yet once a exceeds about 3.57, the orbit no longer repeats and becomes chaotic (with some periodic windows in between); at a = 4, the sequence it produces looks completely random.

This is the most famous example of "deterministic chaos": there is no randomness at all, and the next step is completely determined by the current one, yet at a = 4 it passes linear tests of "is it white noise?" (when a is less than 4, adjacent terms are clearly negatively correlated; for example, at a = 3.8 the correlation coefficient is about −0.6). Here its values are mapped to a price, and the default is a = 4.

zh: 检验"线性的工具看不到非线性的规律"。它的水平值（价格本身的高低）在所有滞后上线性不相关，线性模型却能学到一半：要预测的是水平的增量，而"现在高，接下来多半跌"恰好解释它一半的方差。真相是一条抛物线，k 近邻、树和神经网络可以完全学会。比较各种机器学习模型，这里是最好的场地。
en: To put "linear tools cannot see nonlinear patterns" to the test. Its level (how high or low the price itself is) is linearly uncorrelated at all lags, yet a linear model can still learn half: what has to be predicted is the increment of the level, and "it is high now, so it will most likely fall next" explains exactly half of its variance. The truth is a parabola, which k-nearest neighbors, trees and neural networks can learn completely. For comparing different machine-learning models, this is the best testing ground.

zh: 特征用"价格水平"、滞后数取 1 的非线性模型。验证集的 R² 可以接近 1。
en: A nonlinear model with "Price level" as the feature and the number of lags set to 1. The validation-set R² can come close to 1.

zh: 规则选"预测模型流水线"，特征选"价格水平"，滞后数 1，打开"模型对比"点"开始对比"：线性回归、岭回归和 Lasso 的 R² 停在一半（逻辑回归只猜方向，R² 到 0.72），非线性模型接近 1。
en: Choose the rule "Prediction pipeline", choose the feature "Price level", set the number of lags to 1, open "Model comparison" and click "Start comparison": the R² of linear regression, ridge regression and Lasso stops at one half (logistic regression only guesses the direction, and its R² reaches 0.72), while the nonlinear models come close to 1.

zh: 打开"学到的函数"：真相是一条抛物线，看各个模型的蓝线贴得多近。
en: Open "Learned function": the truth is a parabola; see how closely each model's blue line follows it.

zh: 把观测噪声从 0 调到 0.3：再准的模型也只能预测到被噪声盖住之前的那一部分。
en: Raise the observation noise from 0 to 0.3: however accurate the model, it can predict only the part that was there before the noise covered it.

zh:
1961 年，气象学家 Lorenz 在计算机上模拟一个简化的天气模型。有一次为了省事，他把打印出来的中间结果重新输进去接着算，而打印纸上只保留了三位小数。算出来的"天气"很快就和原来的完全不同。

这就是"蝴蝶效应"的发现：系统是完全确定的，可初始值上极小的差别会指数地放大，长期的预测因此不可能。两年后，他在一个只有三个变量的对流模型（从 Saltzman 的方程简化而来）里重现了同样的现象，发表了那篇著名的论文。这里只让你看到三个变量中的一个。
en:
In 1961 the meteorologist Lorenz was simulating a simplified weather model on a computer. On one occasion, to save trouble, he typed the printed intermediate results back in and continued the computation from there, but the printout kept only three decimal places. The computed "weather" soon became completely different from the original.

This was the discovery of the "butterfly effect": the system is completely deterministic, yet a tiny difference in the initial values is amplified exponentially, so long-term prediction is impossible. Two years later he reproduced the same phenomenon in a convection model with only three variables (simplified from Saltzman's equations) and published the famous paper. Here you are shown only one of the three variables.

zh: 研究两件事。一是"只看得到系统的一部分"时怎么办：Takens 的定理说，用一个变量的若干个滞后值就能重构整个系统的状态，所以"滞后特征 + 非线性模型"是正确的做法。二是预测的时间尺度：一步之后很准，几十步之后和瞎猜一样。
en: To study two things. The first is what to do when "you can see only part of the system": Takens' theorem says that the state of the whole system can be reconstructed from several lagged values of a single variable, so "lagged features + a nonlinear model" is the correct approach. The second is the time scale of prediction: one step ahead it is very accurate, and a few dozen steps ahead it is no better than a blind guess.

zh: 特征用最近几步的"价格水平"，模型用 k 近邻、梯度提升或神经网络。默认的采样间隔下，单棵回归树和随机森林还不如线性回归。
en: Use the "Price level" of the last few steps as the features, and k-nearest neighbors, gradient boosting or a neural network as the model. At the default sampling interval, a single regression tree and a random forest do worse than linear regression.

zh: 规则选"预测模型流水线"，特征选"价格水平"：滞后数取 1 时验证集 R² 接近 0，一个数定不出系统的状态；取 2 时线性回归到 0.79，k 近邻到 0.98。
en: Choose the rule "Prediction pipeline" and the feature "Price level": with the number of lags set to 1 the validation-set R² is close to 0, since one number cannot determine the state of the system; with 2, linear regression reaches 0.79 and k-nearest neighbors reaches 0.98.

zh: 滞后数取 3，把采样间隔 τ 从 0.05 调到 0.2：相邻两个采样点之间的关系变得更弯，线性回归的 R² 从 0.92 掉到 0.24，k 近邻仍在 0.98 以上。
en: Set the number of lags to 3 and change the sampling interval τ from 0.05 to 0.2: the relationship between two adjacent sample points becomes more curved, the R² of linear regression drops from 0.92 to 0.24, and k-nearest neighbors stays above 0.98.

zh: 打开"模型对比"：采样间隔小的时候线性模型也不差；间隔一大，只剩非线性的模型还跟得上。
en: Open "Model comparison": when the sampling interval is small, linear models are not bad either; once the interval is large, only the nonlinear models can still keep up.

zh:
一个挂在弹簧上的重物，被随机的力不断地推：它会以大致固定的周期摆动，但振幅和相位在慢慢漂移。

1927 年，统计学家 Yule 用这个物理图像去描述太阳黑子数的十一年周期，写下了历史上第一个自回归模型。经济里的季节性和商业周期、电力价格的日周期，都是这一类"周期大致固定、但不精确"的信号。
en:
A weight hanging on a spring, pushed continually by a random force: it oscillates with a roughly fixed period, but its amplitude and phase drift slowly.

In 1927 the statistician Yule used this physical picture to describe the eleven-year cycle of sunspot numbers, and wrote down the first autoregressive model in history. Seasonality and business cycles in the economy, and the daily cycle of electricity prices, are all signals of this kind, "with a period that is roughly fixed but not exact".

zh: 研究周期性的信号，以及"模型越简单越好"的情形：这是一个线性的高斯过程，两个滞后的线性回归就是正确答案，更复杂的模型只会多出估计的噪声。
en: To study periodic signals, and a case where "the simpler the model, the better": this is a linear Gaussian process, a linear regression on two lags is the correct answer, and more complex models only add estimation noise.

zh: 两个滞后的线性预测；或者直接利用周期，在低点买、高点卖。
en: A linear prediction from two lags; or using the cycle directly, buying at the lows and selling at the highs.

zh: 规则选"预测模型流水线"，特征选"价格水平"，滞后数 2，打开"模型对比"：线性回归和神经网络并列第一（R² 约 0.88），岭回归和单棵树只有 0.2 上下。两个滞后高度相关、真实系数一正一负，岭回归把它们一起往 0 拉，正好拉坏了。
en: Choose the rule "Prediction pipeline", choose the feature "Price level", set the number of lags to 2, and open "Model comparison": linear regression and the neural network tie for first place (R² about 0.88), while ridge regression and the single tree reach only about 0.2. The two lags are highly correlated and their true coefficients have opposite signs; ridge regression pulls both of them toward 0, and that is exactly what breaks it.

zh: 规则选"均线交叉"：均线的窗口和周期合拍时很好，不合拍时正好买在高点、卖在低点。对两个窗口做二维扫描看这个图案。
en: Choose the rule "Moving-average crossover": it does well when the moving-average windows are in step with the cycle; when they are out of step, it buys right at the highs and sells right at the lows. Run a two-dimensional sweep over the two windows to see this pattern.

zh: 把"每步保留的振幅"从 0.97 调到 0.85：阻尼变大，周期变模糊。线性回归的验证集 R² 从 0.88 掉到 0.5 上下，靠周期吃饭的规则夏普普遍下降；均值回复类的规则（固定阈值带、线性均值回复、网格）增长率反而上升，因为它更像一个普通的均值回复过程了。
en: Change "Amplitude kept per step" from 0.97 to 0.85: the damping increases and the cycle becomes blurred. The validation-set R² of linear regression drops from 0.88 to about 0.5, and the Sharpe ratios of the rules that live off the cycle fall across the board; the growth rates of the mean-reversion rules (fixed threshold bands, linear mean reversion, grid) rise instead, because the process now looks more like an ordinary mean-reverting process.

zh:
模拟的世界再多，最后要面对的是这一个：一段真实发生过的历史。它和所有模拟世界的根本区别是只有一条路径，而且你不知道生成它的规律是什么，甚至不知道这个规律明天还在不在。

页面自带几段旧行情做示范。你可以导入任何一列数字：股票、指数、加密货币的行情，或者一组物理测量值。
en:
However many simulated worlds there are, the one you have to face in the end is this one: a stretch of history that really happened. Its fundamental difference from all the simulated worlds is that there is only one path, and you do not know the law that generated it, or even whether that law will still be there tomorrow.

The page comes with a few stretches of old market data as examples. You can import any column of numbers: prices of stocks, indexes or cryptocurrencies, or a set of physical measurements.

zh: 一个想法在模拟的世界里站住了之后。数据被切成两段：前一段用来调参数，后一段是样本外，留到最后才看。
en: After an idea has held up in the simulated worlds. The data is cut into two segments: the first is used to tune parameters, and the second is out-of-sample, set aside and looked at only at the very end.

zh: 没有"最优"可言，只能问样本外还成不成立。一条历史上的标准误很大：用 $n$ 年的数据估年均收益，标准误是 $\sigma/\sqrt n$，再除以 $\sigma$，夏普比率的标准误就大约是 $1/\sqrt{\text{年数}}$。五年的数据分不清夏普 0.5 和 1.0。
en: There is no "optimum" to speak of; you can only ask whether it still holds out-of-sample. The standard error on a single history is large: when you estimate the average annual return from $n$ years of data, the standard error is $\sigma/\sqrt n$; divide by $\sigma$, and the standard error of the Sharpe ratio is roughly $1/\sqrt{\text{number of years}}$. Five years of data cannot tell a Sharpe ratio of 0.5 from one of 1.0.

zh: 用自带的示例数据跑"均线交叉"，调到满意，再点"揭晓样本外"。
en: Run "Moving-average crossover" on the built-in sample data, tune it until you are satisfied, then click "Reveal out-of-sample".

zh: 把用法换成"滚动窗口"（把这段历史切成很多段互相重叠的小段，每一段当作一条路径）：可以看到分布的形状，但各段互相重叠，标准误偏小。
en: Switch the usage to "Rolling windows" (the history is cut into many short segments that overlap one another, and each segment is treated as one path): you can see the shape of the distribution, but the segments overlap, so the standard error comes out too small.

zh: 打开"价格路径"：阴影的那一段就是留作样本外的。
en: Open "Price paths": the shaded segment is the part set aside as out-of-sample.

zh:
只有一段历史，怎么知道结果里有多少是运气？Efron 1979 年提出的办法叫"自助法"（bootstrap）：把手里的样本当作总体，从里面有放回地重新抽样，抽出很多份"本来也可能发生的历史"。

对时间序列，要一块一块地抽，才能保住短程的相关性。Politis 和 Romano 1994 年让块的长度随机，使抽出的序列保持平稳。
en:
With only one stretch of history, how do you know how much of the result is luck? The method Efron proposed in 1979 is called the "bootstrap": treat the sample in hand as the population and resample from it with replacement, drawing many "histories that could also have happened".

For a time series, you have to draw block by block to preserve the short-range correlation. In 1994 Politis and Romano made the block length random, so that the resampled series remains stationary.

zh: 想要"收益的分布和真实数据一样，又有很多条路径"的时候。它回答的是：同样这些涨跌，换一个先后顺序，这条规则还行吗？
en: When you want "returns distributed like the real data, and many paths as well". The question it answers is: with these same rises and falls in a different order, does the rule still work?

zh: 它保留了真实的厚尾和短程的相关，打乱了块以外的长程结构。把块长取成 1，就是把收益完全洗牌：洗牌前后结果的差距，量出了"时间顺序"本身贡献了多少。
en: It keeps the real heavy tails and the short-range correlation, and scrambles the long-range structure beyond the blocks. Setting the block length to 1 shuffles the returns completely: the gap between the results before and after shuffling measures how much the "time order" itself contributes.

zh: 把平均块长从 10 调到 1：趋势规则的优势如果消失了，说明它靠的是时间顺序里的结构。
en: Change the average block length from 10 to 1: if the advantage of a trend rule disappears, the rule was relying on structure in the time order.

zh: 和"真实数据"世界里同一条规则的结果比：bootstrap 给出的是一个分布，真实历史只是其中的一个点。
en: Compare with the result of the same rule in the "Real data" world: the bootstrap gives a distribution, and the real history is only one point in it.

zh: 内置的世界不够用的时候，可以自己写一个：一段函数，输入步数和随机数发生器，输出一条价格路径。也可以把要求说给 Claude，让它来写。
en: When the built-in worlds are not enough, you can write one yourself: a function that takes the number of steps and a random number generator as input and outputs a price path. You can also tell Claude what you want and let it write the function.

zh: 想检验一个特定的假设，比如"下跌之后波动更高""每年有几次连续多日的暴跌"；或者想把别的领域的模型（物理、生物、排队）拿来当信号源。
en: When you want to test a specific hypothesis, such as "volatility is higher after a fall" or "a few multi-day crashes every year"; or when you want to use a model from another field (physics, biology, queueing) as the signal source.

zh: 取决于你造了什么。先看"价格路径""单步收益分布"和"自相关"三张图，弄清它有什么结构，再选规则。
en: That depends on what you built. First look at the three charts "Price paths", "One-step return distribution" and "Autocorrelation" to find out what structure it has, then choose a rule.

zh: 在 Claude 面板里选"造世界"，输入"带杠杆效应的 GARCH：下跌之后波动更高"。
en: In the Claude panel choose "Build a world" and type "GARCH with a leverage effect: volatility is higher after a fall".

zh: 造好之后，在"世界"一栏点"采样代码与说明"，看它是怎么实现的。
en: Once it is built, click "Sampler code & notes" in the "World" section to see how it is implemented.

zh: 最朴素的规则：不管发生什么，始终让资产占净值的一个固定比例。涨了就卖一点，跌了就买一点，把比例调回去。养老基金常用的"六成股票、四成债券"是它；Kelly 和 Merton 的最优解也是它：在收益独立同分布的世界里，可以证明按长期增长率没有任何规则比一个选对了的固定比例更好。
en: The plainest rule: whatever happens, always keep the asset at a fixed fraction of wealth. When the price rises, sell a little; when it falls, buy a little, to bring the fraction back. The "60% stocks, 40% bonds" mix commonly used by pension funds is this rule; so is the optimal solution of Kelly and Merton: in a world where returns are i.i.d., it can be proved that, measured by long-run growth rate, no rule is better than a correctly chosen fixed fraction.

zh: 收益不可预测（独立同分布、几何布朗运动），并且大致知道 μ 和 σ 的时候。它也是一切规则的参照：别的规则至少要赢过平均仓位和它相同的固定比例。
en: When returns are unpredictable (i.i.d., geometric Brownian motion) and you know μ and σ roughly. It is also the reference for every rule: any other rule should at least beat the fixed fraction with the same average position.

zh: μ 和 σ 估错的时候。μ 尤其难估，估高了就会押得过多，而押得过多比押得不够危险得多，所以实践里常用半 Kelly。在收益可以预测的世界里，它放弃了所有可以利用的信息。
en: When μ and σ are estimated wrongly. μ is especially hard to estimate; overestimate it and you bet too much, and betting too much is far more dangerous than betting too little, so half Kelly is commonly used in practice. In worlds where returns are predictable, it gives up all the information that could be exploited.

zh: 杠杆曲线：峰值在哪里，峰有多平。
en: The leverage curve: where the peak is, and how flat it is.

zh: 买进去，然后什么都不做。1976 年 Bogle 推出第一只面向个人的指数基金（照着一篮子大公司的股票原样买入，不挑不选）时，被同行嘲笑为"甘于平庸"；后来几十年的数据表明，扣除费用之后，多数由基金经理选股、择时的基金跑不赢它。在这里它是价格世界的基准：任何规则的结果，都和它在同一批路径上的结果配对比较。
en: Buy, and then do nothing. When Bogle launched the first index fund for individual investors in 1976 (it buys a basket of large companies' stocks exactly as it is, with no picking and choosing), his peers mocked it as "settling for mediocrity"; the data of the following decades showed that, after fees, most funds whose managers pick stocks and time the market fail to beat it. Here it is the benchmark of the price worlds: the result of every rule is compared with its result on the same batch of paths, in a paired comparison.

zh: 没有可靠的预测、交易成本又不可忽略的时候。
en: When there is no reliable prediction and trading costs are not negligible.

zh: 漂移为负的世界，或者有清晰可预测的结构（均值回复、牛熊切换）的世界。
en: Worlds with negative drift, or worlds with a clear, predictable structure (mean reversion, regime switching).

zh: 它就是结果栏里的"基准"和各张图上的橙线。
en: It is the "Benchmark" in the results bar and the orange line on every chart.

zh:
技术分析（只看过去的价格图形来判断买卖）里资格最老的规则之一。均线是最近若干步价格的平均值，每走一步重算一次。期货交易员 Donchian 从 1960 年起在他的通讯里推广"5 日均线上穿 20 日均线买入，下穿卖出"（短均线从下方升到长均线之上叫上穿，反过来叫下穿），后来的趋势跟踪基金大多从它演化出来。逻辑是：短均线代表最近的价格，长均线代表更早的价格，短的在上面，说明最近在涨。

Brock、Lakonishok 和 LeBaron 1992 年用道琼斯指数近九十年的数据检验了这一类规则，发现买入信号之后的收益确实高于卖出信号之后的。
en:
One of the oldest rules in technical analysis (deciding when to buy and sell by looking only at charts of past prices). A moving average is the average of the prices over the most recent several steps, recomputed at every step. From 1960 on, the futures trader Donchian promoted in his newsletter the rule "buy when the 5-day moving average crosses above the 20-day moving average, sell when it crosses below" (the short moving average rising from below to above the long moving average is called crossing above; the reverse is called crossing below), and most later trend-following funds evolved from it. The logic: the short moving average represents the most recent prices and the long moving average represents earlier prices, so the short one being on top means that prices have been rising recently.

In 1992 Brock, Lakonishok and LeBaron tested this class of rules on nearly ninety years of data on the Dow Jones index and found that the returns after buy signals were indeed higher than the returns after sell signals.

zh: 趋势会持续的世界。H > ½ 的分数布朗运动里它明显赚钱；牛熊切换里它的增长率和买入持有差不多，但回撤小得多、夏普更高。它不预测趋势什么时候开始，只在趋势出现之后跟上去，所以趋势要持续得比均线的窗口长才行。
en: Worlds where trends persist. In fractional Brownian motion with H > ½ it clearly makes money; in the regime-switching world its growth rate is about the same as that of buy and hold, but its drawdown is much smaller and its Sharpe ratio is higher. It does not predict when a trend will start; it only follows once a trend has appeared, so the trend has to last longer than the moving-average window.

zh: 没有趋势的世界里，它白付成本（几何布朗运动）。来回震荡的世界里，它反复被"打脸"：刚买就跌，刚卖就涨（均值回复、带噪谐振子）。
en: In worlds without trends it pays costs for nothing (geometric Brownian motion). In worlds that swing back and forth it gets "whipsawed" again and again: the price falls right after it buys and rises right after it sells (mean reversion, the noisy oscillator).

zh: 单条路径明细里的买卖点；场景对比里它在各个世界的表现；结果栏下面那行小字里的换手。
en: The buy and sell points in the single-path detail chart; how it performs in each world in the scenario comparison; the turnover in the line of small print below the results bar.

zh: 比均线交叉更直接：过去 n 步涨了就做多，跌了就做空。Moskowitz、Ooi 和 Pedersen 2012 年在 58 种期货上发现，过去 12 个月的收益能预测下一个月的收益，在股指、债券、商品、外汇里都成立；他们把它叫作"时间序列动量"。专门在各种期货上做趋势跟踪的基金（管理期货基金），核心策略就是它。
en: More direct than moving-average crossover: go long if the price rose over the past n steps, go short if it fell. In 2012 Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen found, across 58 futures instruments, that the return over the past 12 months predicts the return over the next month, and that this holds for equity indices, bonds, commodities and currencies; they called it "time-series momentum". For the funds that specialize in trend following across all kinds of futures (managed futures funds), it is the core strategy.

zh: 趋势持续得很久的世界，比如 H > ½ 的分数布朗运动。它和均线交叉赚的是同一种钱，但只看首尾两个价格，对窗口的长度更敏感。
en: Worlds where trends last a long time, such as fractional Brownian motion with H > ½. It earns the same kind of profit as moving-average crossover, but it looks only at the first and last prices of the window and is more sensitive to the window length.

zh: 没有趋势或者均值回复的世界。默认允许做空：在漂移为正的世界里，每一次短暂的下跌都让它从做多翻成做空，丢了漂移，还付了成本。牛熊切换里，默认的参数因此输给买入持有；把窗口加长到 60、关掉做空，它就和均线交叉差不多了。
en: Worlds that have no trend or that mean-revert. Shorting is allowed by default: in a world with positive drift, every brief decline flips it from long to short, so it loses the drift and pays costs as well. In the regime-switching world the default parameters lose to buy and hold for this reason; lengthen the window to 60 and turn off shorting, and it becomes about the same as moving-average crossover.

zh: 参数扫描里对窗口 n 的那条曲线。
en: The curve over the window n in the parameter sweep.

zh: 价格偏离它最近的平均水平太远时，赌它回来。"太远"用 z 分数来量：偏离了几个标准差。上世纪 80 年代 Bollinger 把均线上下各两个标准差画成带子，成了看盘软件的标配；同一时期，摩根士丹利的一个小组开始成对地交易相关的股票，价差偏离了就反向下注，这是统计套利的开端。
en: When the price strays too far from its recent average level, bet that it will come back. "Too far" is measured by the z-score: how many standard deviations the price has strayed. In the 1980s Bollinger drew bands two standard deviations above and below the moving average, and they became a standard feature of charting software; in the same period a group at Morgan Stanley began trading correlated stocks in pairs, betting against the move whenever the spread diverged, which was the beginning of statistical arbitrage.

zh: 有东西把价格拉回来的世界：均值回复，Logistic 映射。带噪谐振子里要把窗口取到一到两个半周期（40 到 100 步，每年 +7% 到 +9%；再长又变差，200 步只剩 +3%）；默认的 20 步只有半个周期，价格还在往下摆时它就进场了，每年亏 23%。
en: Worlds where something pulls the price back: mean reversion, the Logistic map. In the noisy oscillator the window has to be set to one to two and a half periods (40 to 100 steps, +7% to +9% per year; longer is worse again, and 200 steps leaves only +3%); the default of 20 steps is only half a period, so it enters while the price is still swinging down, and it loses 23% per year.

zh: 趋势的世界里它逆着趋势进场、一路扛着，行话叫"接飞刀"。跳跃的世界里，一次跳空可能意味着均衡水平本身变了，再也回不来。
en: In trending worlds it enters against the trend and holds on the whole way; in trading jargon this is "catching a falling knife". In worlds with jumps, a single gap may mean that the equilibrium level itself has changed and the price will never come back.

zh: 单条路径明细里它在哪里进场、哪里出场；终值分布的左尾。
en: Where it enters and where it exits in the single-path detail chart; the left tail of the terminal wealth distribution.

zh: 和上一条的区别是：均衡价不是从历史里估的，而是事先知道的。现实里这种情形来自套利关系（同一样东西在两处价格不同，买便宜的、卖贵的）。比如一只跟踪沪深 300 的交易所基金（ETF），一份基金背后是固定的一篮子股票。某一刻这篮股票按市价值 4.00 元，基金在交易所里只卖 3.96 元（数字是示意）。大机构可以拿基金换回这篮股票，所以两个价格迟早合拢：4.00 就是事先知道的均衡价，你要定的是便宜多少才动手。同类的例子：可转债（能按固定比例换成股票的债券）不该比换成股票之后还便宜；港币这样的联系汇率，官方公布了要守住的区间。偏离出一条带子就动手，回到带子里就把仓位调回 0（平仓）。
en: The difference from the previous rule: the equilibrium price is not estimated from history but known in advance. In reality this situation comes from arbitrage relations (the same thing has different prices in two places: buy the cheap one, sell the expensive one). Take an exchange-traded fund (ETF) that tracks the CSI 300: behind each fund share is a fixed basket of stocks. At some moment the basket is worth 4.00 yuan at market prices, while the fund sells on the exchange for only 3.96 yuan (the numbers are illustrative). Large institutions can exchange fund shares for the basket of stocks, so the two prices sooner or later come together: 4.00 is the equilibrium price known in advance, and what you have to decide is how cheap the fund must be before you act. Examples of the same kind: a convertible bond (a bond that can be exchanged for stock at a fixed ratio) should not be cheaper than what it is worth once converted into stock; for a linked exchange rate such as the Hong Kong dollar's, the authorities have announced the range they will defend. Act once the price moves outside a band; once it is back inside the band, bring the position back to 0 (close the position).

zh: 均衡价确实已知、并且不变的均值回复世界。有交易成本时，"带子之外才交易"是理论上正确的形状：每次调仓都要付成本，偏离很小时预期能赚的不够付成本。
en: Mean-reverting worlds where the equilibrium price really is known and does not change. With trading costs, "trade only outside a band" is the theoretically correct shape: every rebalance costs money, and when the deviation is small the expected gain is not enough to pay the cost.

zh: 均衡价会漂移，或者根本不存在的世界。几何布朗运动里，价格一旦离开 100 就不保证回来，它会一直拿着亏损的仓位。
en: Worlds where the equilibrium price drifts, or does not exist at all. In geometric Brownian motion, once the price leaves 100 nothing guarantees that it will come back, and the rule will keep holding a losing position.

zh: 对带宽做参数扫描：太窄则换手太多，太宽则机会太少。
en: Run a parameter sweep over the band width: too narrow and there is too much turnover, too wide and there are too few opportunities.

zh: 一个做价差交易的人已经相信两只股票的价差会回到 θ，半衰期大约两个月。剩下的问题只有一个：偏离 1% 时押多少，偏离 3% 时押多少？这条规则的回答是按偏离的大小成比例加码，不设门槛：仓位随对数价格的偏离线性变化，没有带子，没有阈值。它是均值回复世界（OU 过程）里使长期增长率最高的精确解，是 Merton 那套理论在可预测世界里的延伸。
en: A spread trader already believes that the spread between two stocks will return to θ, with a half-life of about two months. Only one question is left: how much to bet when the deviation is 1%, and how much when it is 3%? This rule's answer is to scale the bet up in proportion to the size of the deviation, with no threshold: the position varies linearly with the deviation of the log price, with no band and no threshold. It is the exact solution that maximizes the long-run growth rate in the mean-reverting world (the OU process), and it is the extension of Merton's theory to a predictable world.

zh: 参数已知、成本很低的均值回复世界。在那里它是可证最优的。
en: Mean-reverting worlds where the parameters are known and costs are very low. There it is provably optimal.

zh: 它每一步都在调仓，默认设定下一年的换手是净值的七十多倍，成本一大就被吃光。参数估错（尤其是均衡价）时，它会坚定地朝错误的方向下重注。
en: It rebalances at every step; with the default settings its turnover in one year is more than seventy times wealth, and as soon as costs are large they eat up everything it earns. When the parameters are misestimated (the equilibrium price especially), it bets heavily, and with conviction, in the wrong direction.

zh: 和"固定阈值带"对照：交易成本是 0 时它遥遥领先（每年 40% 对 19%）；把成本调到 60 个基点，它由盈转亏（−5%），带子规则只从 19% 降到 14%。
en: Compare with "Fixed threshold bands": when the trading cost is 0 it is far ahead (40% per year versus 19%); raise the cost to 60 basis points and it goes from a profit to a loss (−5%), while the band rule only drops from 19% to 14%.

zh:
不预测方向，只管理风险：波动高的时候减仓，低的时候加仓，让组合的波动大致恒定。风险平价基金（比如桥水 1996 年推出的"全天候"组合）把"按风险、而不是按金额分配仓位"的思路带进了主流；Moreira 和 Muir 2017 年的论文表明，在美国股市近百年的数据上，按上个月的波动调仓位能提高夏普比率。

道理是：波动可以预测（它会聚集），而期望收益并不随波动同步升高。所以高波动的时期，是"风险大而报酬不多"的时期。
en:
It does not predict direction; it only manages risk: reduce the position when volatility is high and add to it when volatility is low, so that the portfolio's volatility stays roughly constant. Risk-parity funds (for example the "All Weather" portfolio that Bridgewater launched in 1996) brought the idea of "allocating positions by risk rather than by amount of money" into the mainstream; a 2017 paper by Moreira and Muir showed that, on nearly a hundred years of US stock market data, adjusting the position according to the previous month's volatility raises the Sharpe ratio.

The reasoning: volatility is predictable (it clusters), while expected return does not rise in step with volatility. So high-volatility periods are periods of "high risk but not much reward".

zh: 波动会聚集、而且高波动并不带来更高收益的世界。牛熊切换里最明显：熊市波动高、收益为负，它躲开了一大半，夏普从 0.61 升到 1.14。Heston 的默认参数下夏普略有改善（0.44 对 0.40）；GARCH 的默认参数下波动的起伏不够大，好处被估计的噪声抵掉，夏普和买入持有分不出高低（0.37 对 0.39）。两处它主要都是把回撤降下来。
en: Worlds where volatility clusters and high volatility does not bring higher returns. It is clearest in the regime-switching world: bear markets have high volatility and negative returns, it avoids the greater part of them, and the Sharpe ratio rises from 0.61 to 1.14. With Heston's default parameters the Sharpe ratio improves slightly (0.44 versus 0.40); with GARCH's default parameters volatility does not swing widely enough, the benefit is canceled by estimation noise, and its Sharpe ratio cannot be told apart from that of buy and hold (0.37 versus 0.39). In both places what it mainly does is bring the drawdown down.

zh: 波动恒定的世界（几何布朗运动）：估出来的波动变化全是噪声，跟着它调仓只是多付成本。跳跃的世界：波动是事后才升高的，减仓时已经晚了。
en: Worlds with constant volatility (geometric Brownian motion): the changes in the estimated volatility are pure noise, and rebalancing to follow them only pays extra costs. Worlds with jumps: volatility rises only after the fact, and by the time the position is reduced it is already too late.

zh: 最大回撤分布（它主要改善的是这个）；杠杆曲线。
en: The max drawdown distribution (this is what it mainly improves); the leverage curve.

zh: 交易员最熟悉的纪律：亏到一定程度就认输离场，免得小亏变成大亏。它值不值得，取决于世界。Kaminski 和 Lo（2014）的研究给了一个干净的结论：价格是随机游走时，止损降低期望收益；价格有动量，或者在好坏两种状态之间切换时，止损有正的价值。
en: The discipline traders know best: when the loss reaches a certain level, admit defeat and get out, so that a small loss does not become a large one. Whether it is worth it depends on the world. The study by Kaminski and Lo (2014) gives a clean result: when the price is a random walk, a stop-loss lowers the expected return; when the price has momentum, or switches between a good state and a bad state, a stop-loss has positive value.

zh: 下跌会持续的世界：牛熊切换，有趋势的世界。
en: Worlds where declines persist: regime switching, worlds with trends.

zh: 均值回复的世界：它恰好卖在最低点，然后看着价格涨回去。几何布朗运动：止损之后空仓的那段时间，白白错过了正的漂移。跳空：价格直接越过止损线，成交在更差的位置。
en: Mean-reverting worlds: it sells right at the lowest point and then watches the price climb back. Geometric Brownian motion: during the time it is flat after a stop-loss, it misses the positive drift for nothing. Gaps: the price goes straight past the stop-loss line, and the trade is filled at a worse price.

zh: 单条路径明细里止损和再入场的位置；最大回撤分布，对照买入持有。
en: Where the stop-loss and the re-entry occur in the single-path detail chart; the max drawdown distribution, compared with buy and hold.

zh:
一只承诺"三年后至少还你本金"的基金，手里的 100 元多少敢放进股票？1987 年 Black 和 Jones 提出的"固定比例组合保险"给了一个办法：先定一条不能跌破的底线，把净值高出底线的部分（安全垫）放大若干倍投进风险资产。净值涨，安全垫变厚，仓位自动加大；净值跌，仓位自动缩小，贴近底线时几乎空仓。保本基金用的就是它。

它的近亲"组合保险"在 1987 年的股灾里出了名：很多机构同时按规则卖出，加剧了下跌。
en:
A fund has promised "you get at least your principal back in three years": how much of the 100 yuan it holds does it dare put into stocks? In 1987 Black and Jones proposed "constant-proportion portfolio insurance", which gives one way to do it: first set a floor that wealth must not fall below, then scale up the part of wealth above the floor (the cushion) by some multiple and invest that amount in the risky asset. When wealth rises, the cushion gets thicker and the position grows automatically; when wealth falls, the position shrinks automatically, and close to the floor it is almost flat. This is what principal-protected funds use.

Its close relative, "portfolio insurance", became well known in the 1987 stock market crash: many institutions sold at the same time as their rules required, which deepened the fall.

zh: 有硬性底线的资金。趋势明显的市场里，它在上涨中越买越多。
en: Money that has a hard floor. In a market with a clear trend, it buys more and more as prices rise.

zh: 来回震荡的市场：它涨了买、跌了卖，每个来回都在高买低卖。跳空：价格一步跌穿安全垫，底线就守不住了。
en: Markets that swing back and forth: it buys after a rise and sells after a fall, so on every round trip it buys high and sells low. Gaps: if the price falls through the cushion in a single step, the floor can no longer be held.

zh: 终值分布（左边被截在底线附近）；最大回撤分布。
en: The terminal wealth distribution (cut off on the left near the floor); the max drawdown distribution.

zh:
Kelly 公式需要 μ 和 σ，可现实里没人告诉你它们是多少。这条规则用过去 n 步的数据去估，再打个折扣下注。

它把一个常被忽略的事实摆到了台面上：μ 极难估准。用 n 年的数据估年化的漂移，标准误是 $\sigma/\sqrt n$；波动 20% 时，十年的数据给出的 μ 也有 ±6% 的误差，和 μ 本身差不多大。
en:
The Kelly formula needs μ and σ, but in reality nobody tells you what they are. This rule estimates them from the data of the past n steps and then bets at a discount.

It puts a commonly overlooked fact on the table: μ is extremely hard to estimate accurately. When the annualized drift is estimated from n years of data, the standard error is $\sigma/\sqrt n$; with volatility at 20%, even ten years of data give μ with an error of ±6%, about as large as μ itself.

zh: 参数缓慢变化、需要跟着调整的世界。也用它当作"不知道参数时，固定比例能做到多好"的现实版参照。
en: Worlds where the parameters change slowly and you have to adjust along with them. Also use it as the realistic reference for "how well a fixed fraction can do when the parameters are not known".

zh: 窗口短的时候它追着噪声跑：刚涨过就加仓，刚跌过就减仓，变成一个劣质的动量规则。
en: With a short window it chases noise: it adds to the position right after a rise and reduces it right after a fall, and becomes a low-quality momentum rule.

zh: 对窗口 n 和收缩系数做二维扫描；和知道真实参数的"固定比例"对照，差距就是"不知道参数"的代价。
en: Run a two-dimensional sweep over the window n and the shrinkage factor; compare with a "Fixed fraction" that knows the true parameters: the gap is the price of "not knowing the parameters".

zh: 在锚定价的上下每隔一段距离设一档：每跌一格多买一份，每涨一格卖出一份。外汇和加密货币的散户里很流行，各种"网格交易机器人"做的就是这个。它是做市商（同时挂出一个买价和一个稍高的卖价、随时愿意和人成交的交易者）的简化版：靠价格来回波动，赚格子之间的差价。
en: Set a level at regular intervals above and below the anchor price: buy one more unit each time the price falls by one grid level, and sell one unit each time it rises by one grid level. It is popular among retail traders in foreign exchange and cryptocurrencies, and it is what the various "grid trading bots" do. It is a simplified version of a market maker (a trader who posts a bid price and a slightly higher ask price at the same time and is willing to trade with anyone at any moment): it relies on the price moving back and forth and earns the price difference between grid levels.

zh: 在一个区间里来回震荡的世界：均值回复，带噪谐振子。
en: Worlds that swing back and forth within a range: mean reversion, the noisy oscillator.

zh: 一直朝一个方向走的行情。一路跌，它一路买，库存越积越多、亏得越来越深；一路涨，它早早卖光，后面的涨幅和它无关。
en: Markets that keep moving in one direction. When the price falls all the way, it buys all the way down, its inventory piles up and its losses get deeper and deeper; when the price rises all the way, it sells out early, and the rest of the rise has nothing to do with it.

zh: 单条路径明细里仓位随价格阶梯状地变化；终值分布的左尾。
en: The position changing in a staircase pattern with the price in the single-path detail chart; the left tail of the terminal wealth distribution.

zh:
输了就把赌注加倍，赢一次就能把前面的亏损全部捞回，还净赚一份。18 世纪的法国赌场里就有人这么玩，这种押法叫 martingale（马丁格尔），名字也是那时候来的；数学里的"鞅"是同一个词。

它的问题是：连输的次数没有上限，而本金有。每一轮小赢的背后，都藏着一次输光的可能；两者的期望恰好抵消，赌局不利时还要倒贴。把它放在这里，是因为它的净值曲线在出事之前非常好看。
en:
Double the stake after every loss; a single win then recovers all the earlier losses and nets one unit on top. People were already playing this way in French casinos in the 18th century; this way of betting is called the martingale, and the name dates from that time too; the "martingale" of mathematics is the same word.

Its problem: there is no upper limit on the number of consecutive losses, but there is one on your capital. Behind every round of small winnings hides the possibility of losing everything once; the expectations of the two cancel exactly, and when the game is unfavorable you end up paying on top of that. It is included here because its wealth curve looks very good until something goes wrong.

zh: 没有。它是用来认识一种风险形态的：多数时候小赚，偶尔一次亏光。
en: None. It is here so that you can get to know one shape of risk: small gains most of the time, and now and then a total loss.

zh: 收益互相独立的世界里都不行；在有优势的赌局里，它也不如固定比例。例外是一步反转很强的世界（Logistic 映射里每年 +7%）：亏了加倍在那里碰巧是一条反转规则。那是世界的结构送的，不是加倍的功劳。
en: It fails in every world where returns are independent of each other; in a game where you have an edge, it is also worse than a fixed fraction. The exception is a world with strong one-step reversal (+7% per year in the Logistic map): there, doubling after a loss happens to be a reversal rule. That is a gift from the world's structure, not the merit of doubling.

zh: 终值分布最左端的那根柱子；最大回撤分布；结果栏下面那行小字里的破产概率。再和它的夏普比率对照着看。
en: The leftmost bar of the terminal wealth distribution; the max drawdown distribution; the ruin probability in the line of small print below the results bar. Then look at these side by side with its Sharpe ratio.

zh:
量化基金里标准的三段式流程：先从历史里提取特征，再用模型预测下一步的收益，最后把预测换算成仓位。这条规则把三段都做成了可以换的零件：特征有三组，模型有十种（从"永远猜平均数"到神经网络），仓位的换算有两种。

它的用处是让你在同一个世界里，把不同的建模方法并排比一比。
en:
The standard three-stage workflow at a quant fund: first extract features from history, then use a model to predict the next step's return, and finally convert the prediction into a position. This rule makes all three stages interchangeable parts: there are three sets of features, ten models (from "always guess the mean" to a neural network) and two ways of converting the prediction into a position.

Its use is to let you compare different modeling approaches side by side in the same world.

zh: 有可以预测的结构的世界。AR(1)、带噪谐振子里，线性模型就够了；Logistic 映射、洛伦兹系统里，需要非线性的模型。均值回复世界里要把特征换成"价格水平"（规律在水平里，换了之后每年 +28%）；默认的特征是最近几步的收益，在那里学不到东西，每年亏 4%。
en: Worlds with predictable structure. In AR(1) and the noisy oscillator a linear model is enough; in the Logistic map and the Lorenz system a nonlinear model is needed. In the mean-reversion world the features have to be switched to "Price level" (the pattern is in the level; after the switch it earns +28% per year); the default features are the returns of the last few steps, from which nothing can be learned there, and it loses 4% per year.

zh: 没有结构的世界：灵活的模型会在训练集上"学到"并不存在的规律，然后照着它去交易。训练数据和交易数据的规律不一样（非平稳）时，学到的函数会过期。
en: Worlds without structure: a flexible model will "learn" patterns on the training set that do not exist and then trade on them. When the patterns in the training data and in the trading data are not the same (nonstationarity), the learned function goes out of date.

zh: 先看"模型诊断"里的验证集 R²，再看净值。"模型对比"把十种模型排在一起，连同各自的训练用时和模型大小。
en: First look at the validation-set R² in "Model diagnostics", then at wealth. "Model comparison" lines up the ten models side by side, along with each one's training time and model size.

zh:
1960 年 Kalman 发表的滤波算法，几年之内就用在了阿波罗飞船的导航上：飞船的真实位置看不到，只有带噪声的测量；滤波器把"按物理规律推算的位置"和"测量到的位置"按各自的可信程度加权平均。

这里把"当前的期望收益"当作那个看不到的位置：它在慢慢地游走，每一步的实际收益是对它的一次带噪声的测量。
en:
The filtering algorithm that Kalman published in 1960 was in use within a few years for the navigation of the Apollo spacecraft: the spacecraft's true position cannot be seen, and there are only noisy measurements; the filter takes a weighted average of "the position extrapolated from the laws of physics" and "the measured position", each weighted by how reliable it is.

Here the "current expected return" is treated as that unseen position: it wanders slowly, and each step's realized return is one noisy measurement of it.

zh: 期望收益缓慢变化的世界：牛熊切换，分数布朗运动。它是"滚动平均"的最优版本：新数据该占多大的权重，由信号和噪声的相对大小决定。这里这个权重由"有效记忆长度"给定，要靠参数扫描去找。
en: Worlds where the expected return changes slowly: regime switching, fractional Brownian motion. It is the optimal version of a "rolling average": how much weight new data should get is determined by the relative sizes of the signal and the noise. Here that weight is set by "Effective memory length" and has to be found by a parameter sweep.

zh: 期望收益不变的世界里，它跟踪的是噪声。期望收益突变而不是渐变时，它反应太慢。
en: In worlds where the expected return does not change, what it tracks is noise. When the expected return changes abruptly rather than gradually, it reacts too slowly.

zh: 对"有效记忆长度"做参数扫描。
en: Run a parameter sweep over "Effective memory length".

zh:
隐马尔可夫模型假定世界在几个看不见的状态之间切换，每个状态下数据有不同的分布。上世纪 70 年代它成了语音识别的支柱（看不见的状态是音素，看得见的是声波）；Hamilton 1989 年把它引进经济学，用来识别扩张和衰退。

这条规则用它识别牛市和熊市：先在训练路径上估出两个状态各自的涨幅、波动和持续时间；交易时每走一步，就更新一次"现在是牛市的概率"。
en:
A hidden Markov model assumes that the world switches among a few unseen states, and that the data have a different distribution in each state. In the 1970s it became the backbone of speech recognition (the unseen states are phonemes, and what is seen is the sound wave); in 1989 Hamilton brought it into economics to identify expansions and recessions.

This rule uses it to identify bull and bear markets: it first estimates, on the training paths, each of the two states' rate of rise, volatility and duration; then, while trading, it updates "the probability that it is a bull market now" at every step.

zh: 牛熊切换的世界。在那里它假设的结构恰好就是数据真实的生成方式（统计里叫"正确设定"），应当赢过均线和动量。
en: The regime-switching world. There the structure it assumes is exactly the way the data are really generated (in statistics this is called "correctly specified"), and it should beat moving averages and momentum.

zh: 没有状态的世界里，它照样会"识别"出两个状态，那是在给噪声分类。状态切换得很快，或者两个状态差别不大时，它确认得太慢。
en: In worlds with no states it will still "identify" two states; it is then classifying noise. When the states switch very quickly, or when the two states differ little, it is too slow to confirm a switch.

zh: 规则下方显示的拟合结果，和左栏世界的真实参数对一对；"模型诊断"。
en: The fitted parameters shown below the rule, checked against the world's true parameters in the left column; "Model diagnostics".

zh:
不事先训练，边走边学：每一步先预测，看到真实的结果之后，朝着减小误差的方向把模型的系数挪一小步。Widrow 和 Hoff 1960 年为自适应滤波器发明了这个办法，电话线路里的回声消除用的就是它。

它的理论保证来自在线学习：不对数据做任何概率假设，累计的预测损失也不会比事后看来最好的那个固定模型差太多。
en:
No training in advance; it learns as it goes: at each step it first predicts, and after seeing the actual outcome it moves the model's coefficients a small step in the direction that reduces the error. Widrow and Hoff invented this method in 1960 for adaptive filters, and it is what echo cancellation on telephone lines uses.

Its theoretical guarantee comes from online learning: with no probabilistic assumption on the data at all, the cumulative prediction loss is still not much worse than that of the fixed model that turns out best in hindsight.

zh: 没有历史数据可以预先训练，或者规律在慢慢变的时候。计算和存储都极省：每一步只做几次乘法，只记几个数。
en: When there is no historical data to train on in advance, or when the pattern is slowly changing. It is extremely economical in both computation and memory: each step takes only a few multiplications and keeps only a few numbers.

zh: 信噪比很低时，它在一条路径里见到的数据太少，学不出东西。同一个世界里，它远不如把所有训练路径汇总起来估计的线性回归。
en: When the signal-to-noise ratio is very low, it sees too little data within a single path to learn anything. In the same world it is far worse than a linear regression estimated by pooling all the training paths.

zh: 对学习率做参数扫描；和"预测模型流水线"里的线性回归对照。
en: Run a parameter sweep over the learning rate; compare with the linear regression in "Prediction pipeline".

zh:
场景是这样的：信号在零附近来回翻，每翻一次都调仓，利润全交了手续费。什么时候该按兵不动？这条规则不把答案写死，让程序自己试出来：不告诉它任何做法，只让它反复尝试，赚了就加强刚才的做法，亏了就削弱。Watkins 1989 年提出的 Q-learning 是强化学习里最基本的算法。它学的是一张表，记着"在每种状态下做每个动作，长期能得到多少回报"。

这里的状态是"价格相对均线的位置"和"当前的持仓"，动作是做多、空仓、做空，交易成本直接算在回报里。
en:
The scenario is this: the signal flips back and forth around zero, the position is rebalanced at every flip, and all the profit goes to fees. When should you stay put? This rule does not hard-code the answer and lets the program find it by trial: it is not told what to do at all and only tries again and again; when it makes money, what it just did is reinforced, and when it loses, that is weakened. Q-learning, proposed by Watkins in 1989, is the most basic algorithm in reinforcement learning. What it learns is a table that records "how much reward you get in the long run from taking each action in each state".

Here the state is "where the price is relative to its moving average" together with "the current position"; the actions are long, flat and short, and trading costs are counted directly in the reward.

zh: 交易成本不可忽略、需要学会"什么时候不动"的情形。它学出来的表里会自己出现一条"不交易带"。
en: Situations where trading costs are not negligible and the rule has to learn "when to stay put". A "no-trade band" appears on its own in the table it learns.

zh: 它需要的数据比有监督的模型多得多；状态稍微多一点，表就填不满。没有结构的世界里，它学到的是一张随机的表。
en: It needs far more data than a supervised model; with only slightly more states, the table cannot be filled. In a world without structure, what it learns is a random table.

zh:
同一个问题往往有好几种算法。除了"结果好不好"，还有几件事决定一个算法能不能用、值不值得用：

- **事先要算多少（训练）。** 决定了能喂给它多少数据、多久能重新训练一次。
- **每一步要算多少（决策）。** 日线级别的交易无所谓；做市和高频里，决策要在微秒之内完成，每步的计算量就是生死线。回测时它决定了能跑多少条路径。
- **要记住多少东西（存储）。** 一个"在线"的算法，每来一个数据只更新几个数，存储不随时间增长；有的算法要把全部历史留着。
- **需要什么数据。** 有的规则只用眼前的价格，有的要一段回看窗口，有的要一大批训练路径，有的要事先知道分布。需要的越多，现实里越难满足。
- **有几个可调的参数。** 参数越多，越容易把这一批数据的偶然性调进去。
- **有没有保证。** 规则说明里的档位：可证最优、族内最优、有保证、启发式。四个词的意思见"名词"。

**记号。** $T$：一条路径的步数或一局的回合数。$w$：回看窗口的长度。$n$：训练样本数。$d$：特征个数。$k$：近邻数。$B$：树的棵数。$h$：树的深度。$H$：隐层宽度。$E$：训练轮数。$I$：迭代次数。$S$：隐状态的个数。$K$：老虎机的台数。$G$：格点数。$O(\cdot)$ 的意思见"名词"里的时间复杂度。
en:
The same problem often has several algorithms. Besides "how good the result is", a few other things decide whether an algorithm can be used and whether it is worth using:

- **How much has to be computed in advance (training).** This determines how much data you can feed it and how often you can retrain it.
- **How much has to be computed at each step (decision).** For trading on daily bars it does not matter; in market making and high-frequency trading a decision has to be made within microseconds, and the amount of computation per step is a matter of life and death. In a backtest it determines how many paths you can run.
- **How much has to be remembered (memory).** An "online" algorithm updates only a few numbers each time a data point arrives, and its memory does not grow with time; some algorithms have to keep the entire history.
- **What data it needs.** Some rules use only the current price, some need a lookback window, some need a large batch of training paths, and some need to know the distribution in advance. The more a rule needs, the harder it is to satisfy in reality.
- **How many tunable parameters it has.** The more parameters there are, the easier it is to tune the accidental features of this batch of data into them.
- **Whether it has a guarantee.** The tier in a rule's notes: provably optimal, optimal in its family, guaranteed, heuristic. For what the four terms mean, see "Glossary".

**Notation.** $T$: the number of steps in a path or the number of rounds in an episode. $w$: the length of the lookback window. $n$: the number of training samples. $d$: the number of features. $k$: the number of neighbors. $B$: the number of trees. $h$: the depth of a tree. $H$: the width of the hidden layer. $E$: the number of training epochs. $I$: the number of iterations. $S$: the number of hidden states. $K$: the number of bandit arms. $G$: the number of grid points. For what $O(\cdot)$ means, see time complexity in "Glossary".

zh: **怎么读这张表。** "滚动统计"一类的规则每一步只做固定的几次运算（均值和标准差用滑动求和维护，不必每次把窗口重算一遍），但要留着最近 $w$ 个数。"公式"和"状态机"一类大多连窗口都不用（例外是"止损与再入场"：等着再入场时要看最近 $w$ 步的最高价）：状态机只记着"现在处于哪种情形"的几个标记（有没有持仓、是不是在等再入场），每一步按标记和新价格决定动作。带训练的规则把计算挪到了事先（表里叫"离线"：在一批数据上一次算好）：训练可以很重，训练完之后每一步往往很轻。这张表里的 $w$ 是规则回看的步数，就是各条规则参数里的"窗口"。
en: **How to read this table.** Rules of the "Rolling statistics" type do only a fixed handful of operations at each step (the mean and the standard deviation are maintained with sliding sums, so the window does not have to be recomputed every time), but they have to keep the last $w$ numbers. Rules of the "Formula" and "State machine" types mostly do not even use a window (the exception is "Stop-loss and re-entry": while waiting to re-enter it has to look at the highest price of the last $w$ steps): a state machine remembers only a few flags for "which situation it is in now" (whether it holds a position, whether it is waiting to re-enter), and at each step it decides the action from the flags and the new price. Rules with training move the computation ahead of time (the table calls this "offline": computed once on a batch of data): training can be heavy, and after training each step is often light. The $w$ in this table is the number of steps a rule looks back, that is, the "window" in each rule's parameters.

zh: **怎么读这张表。** 从上到下，模型越来越灵活，代价也越来越大。两个极端值得记住：线性回归把 $n$ 个样本压成了 $d+1$ 个数，预测只要 $d$ 次乘法；k 近邻什么都不压缩，把训练样本原样背在身上，预测时现找邻居。单棵树的预测只走 $h$ 步，和线性模型一样是几十纳秒的事；成片的树要把 $B$ 棵都走一遍，在这里是几微秒，比线性模型慢两个数量级，但仍比 k 近邻现找邻居快。具体的数字看"模型对比"图下面的表，那是在你的设备上量出来的。
en: **How to read this table.** From top to bottom the models become more and more flexible, and also more and more costly. Two extremes are worth remembering: linear regression compresses $n$ samples into $d+1$ numbers, and a prediction takes only $d$ multiplications; k-nearest neighbors compresses nothing, carries the training samples around as they are, and looks for neighbors on the spot at prediction time. A prediction from a single tree takes only $h$ steps and, as with a linear model, is a matter of tens of nanoseconds; an ensemble of trees has to walk through all $B$ of them, which here takes a few microseconds, two orders of magnitude slower than a linear model but still faster than k-nearest neighbors looking for neighbors on the spot. For the actual numbers, see the table below the "Model comparison" chart; they are measured on your device.

zh: **怎么读这张表。** 四十多条规则里，大多数每一步只做固定的几次运算、什么都不用记，表里写的就是 $O(1)$。有看头的是剩下的那些，能看到几种典型的取舍。动态规划（接单、偏硬币）把整个问题事先算完，存成一张表，之后每一步只是查表：事先算得多、存得多，现场什么都不用想。"从历史里学"的报童规则相反：不用事先算，但把全部历史都存着，越往后越慢；换成"随机逼近"的写法，每步只更新一个数，就不随时间增长了。老虎机的几个算法每步都只扫一遍各台机器，差别全在"怎么打分"上，而不在计算量上。
en: **How to read this table.** Of the forty-odd rules, most do only a fixed handful of operations at each step and need to remember nothing, and the table shows $O(1)$ for them. The ones worth looking at are the rest, where several typical trade-offs can be seen. Dynamic programming (job offers, biased coin) works the whole problem out in advance and stores it as a table, after which each step is only a table lookup: much is computed and stored in advance, and nothing has to be thought about on the spot. The newsvendor rule "Learn from history" is the opposite: nothing is computed in advance, but it keeps the entire history and gets slower and slower as time goes on; written instead in "stochastic approximation" form, it updates only one number per step and no longer grows with time. The bandit algorithms all make only one pass over the arms at each step; they differ entirely in "how to score" and not in the amount of computation.

zh:
**实测的数字在哪里。** 理论上的 $O(\cdot)$ 只说增长的快慢，不说具体多少。页面在你自己的设备上量了三样东西：

- 左栏规则下面的一行小字。"每步决策约 97 纳秒"：规则每做一次决定平均用的时间（一纳秒是十亿分之一秒，一微秒是一千纳秒）。"不带状态"：规则不用在两步之间记任何东西；"开局时自带状态 3 个数"：规则有一个自己的记事本，开局时里面有 3 个数，之后每一步都可以改写它。"模型 12 个数，训练用了 8 毫秒"：带训练的规则事先拟合出来的模型由多少个数组成、拟合用了多久。
- "多策略对比"的表里，最后两列是每条规则的每步用时和模型大小。
- "模型对比"图下面的表：十种模型各自的训练用时、预测一次的用时、存了多少个数。

每步用时里包含了回测引擎本身的开销（几十纳秒），所以很轻的规则之间差别不大；带模型的规则才会拉开数量级。
en:
**Where the measured numbers are.** The theoretical $O(\cdot)$ says only how fast the cost grows, not how much it actually is. The page measures three things on your own device:

- The line of small print below the rule in the left column. "Decision time per step: about 97 ns": the average time the rule takes each time it makes a decision (one nanosecond is one billionth of a second, and one microsecond is one thousand nanoseconds). "Stateless": the rule does not need to remember anything between two steps; "Initial state: 3 numbers": the rule has a notebook of its own, which holds 3 numbers at the start and which it may rewrite at every step after that. "Model: 12 numbers, training took 8 ms": how many numbers make up the model that a rule with training fits in advance, and how long the fit took.
- In the "Strategy comparison" table, the last two columns are each rule's time per step and model size.
- The table below the "Model comparison" chart: for each of the ten models, the training time, the time for one prediction and how many numbers it stores.

The time per step includes the overhead of the backtest engine itself (tens of nanoseconds), so there is little difference among very light rules; only rules with models pull apart by orders of magnitude.
